_comment: The textbook's slip named correctly: the number is an odds ratio and estimates the relative risk only because the disease is rare.

stem.en: The textbook reports that smokers had a risk of lung cancer 8.1 times that of non-smokers. Which description of the number 8.1 is correct?

text.en: It is an odds ratio, and it estimates the relative risk fairly here because lung cancer was rare
It is a relative risk, worked out directly from the two exposure rates in the table
It is an odds ratio, and an odds ratio can never be used to estimate a relative risk
It is the risk of lung cancer among smokers, 8.1 per cent, compared with the risk in non-smokers

explanation.en: The cross-product ad/bc builds an odds ratio, not a relative risk, because the study starts from people who already have the disease. When the disease is rare, the odds ratio sits close to the relative risk a cohort study would measure, so it is a fair estimate here. It is not a percentage and it is not a risk.

hints.en: Ask what the two exposure rates can give, and what the cross-product actually divides.
